title: Delta Frame Assertions — Streaming SDK PRD (sketch)
summary: Sketch PRD proposing a lightweight streaming envelope ("delta-frames") with explicit semantic assertions and an SDK surface that makes partial structured results first-class. Goal: reduce client parsing pain, improve graceful degradation, and make tool-calling deterministic under bandwidth/latency constraints.
goals: 1) Provide a canonical streaming frame envelope that carries both incremental text and explicit structured assertions (checks) developers can rely on. 2) Define SDK ergonomics for mobile and server clients to consume partial structured outputs safely. 3) Specify a tool-calling registry and typed handshake to avoid ambiguous tool resolution when responses arrive incrementally. 4) Include operator controls: assertion strictness, fallback model routing, and metrics for perceptual quality regressions.
background: We have many internal PRDs focused on progressive streaming and tool-handshake patterns. Those documents explore partial JSON frames, typed tool contracts, and resumable sessions. This proposal takes a different angle: make assertions (semantic metadata about partial content) a first-class part of the stream so clients can make safe local decisions (render, prompt, call tool) without waiting for the final token stream. Use-case examples: incremental search result synthesis that triggers enrichment tools as relevant snippets arrive; mobile UIs that show conservative card summaries early and replace them when an assertion upgrades; server-side tool chains that hedge between fast cheap models and slower exacting ones using assertion confidence scores.
proposed_solution: Introduce a small, backwards-compatible streaming envelope we call 'delta-frame assertion' (DFA). Each DFA frame is an independent JSON object (JSONL over the stream) with a header and optional typed payloads: textual delta, structured delta, assertion block, and tool-call hint. Frames are orderable by sequence id and idempotent (clients can replay). Assertions are typed labels (e.g., 'intent:recommendation', 'entities:invoice'), each with a confidence score, optional schema id, and a validity window indicating if it can be acted on early or must be confirmed by a later 'commit' frame. The SDK surfaces helpers: typed parsers, optimistic render components, and an assert-evaluator that decides "safe to act" using configurable thresholds.
sdk_patterns: Client SDKs expose two primary primitives: (A) StreamCursor: an async iterator over DFA frames with helpers to group frames by logical episodes (session fragment ids); (B) AssertEvaluator: a small rule engine that combines assertion scores, schema contracts, and local policy (latency budget, user preference) to produce an 'act' decision. Higher-level helpers: 'optimisticRenderer' that shows partial structured cards and marks them as 'tentative' while waiting for a commit frame; 'toolDispatcher' that debounces and hedges tool calls (e.g., call a fast parser locally, send a queued tool invocation server-side if the assertion upgrades). Mobile SDKs add 'bandwidthMode' that tightens actionability thresholds and collapses low-confidence assertions into a single 'needs-confirmation' placeholder. Server SDKs offer a 'pipeline mode' to chain tool calls with auto-fallback to lighter models when assertion confidence is low.
tool_calling: We propose a minimal tool registry concept: tools register id+semantic interface+capabilities (sync/async, required_schema). Tool hints in frames reference tool ids and include 'intent_score' and 'expected_cost' so the client or the platform can decide local vs server-side invocation. A tool 'handshake' event (non-stream frame) begins the canonical call if the client chooses to act; responses from tools stream back as DFA frames with their own assertion envelopes, enabling nested incremental flows. To avoid races, tool calls carry 'parent_frame_id' and 'expected_commit_seq' so results map deterministically back to the session state.
operator_controls: Server-side config knobs: assertion-strictness (float 0-1), optimistic-mode toggle, per-route tool-call budget, and auto-fallback routing (e.g., route to cheaper model when assertion entropy high). Observability: expose assertion-distribution histograms, time-to-first-assertion, tool-invocation-latency, and pct of optimistic-acted frames that later downgraded to 'invalid' — important for measuring perceptual regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs (JS + Python + iOS) can parse DFA streams and surface StreamCursor + AssertEvaluator. 2) Demo app: live chat UI that renders tentative action cards and performs a safe tool call (invoice extraction) with rollback when commit invalidates. 3) Platform: support for tool registry metadata and ability to throttle tool hints per route. 4) Telemetry: assertion histograms and rollback rate are visible in Console for the demo route.
success_metrics: - Time-to-first-assertion median < 200ms for 95th percentile of requests. - Tool invocation error/rollback rate < 1.5% for opt-in flows. - Client perceived latency (time until first tentative card) improvement > 30% vs naive final-only render. - Number of customer projects adopting DFA within 3 months of SDK GA (target: 5 internal+2 external pilots).
risk_mitigation: - Backwards compatibility: frames are optional and ignored by legacy clients; platform will continue to emit standard streaming text frames. - Safety: default policy is conservative (do not auto-invoke tools unless assertion confidence > 0.9). - Complexity: start with small number of assertion types (intent, entities, schema references) and iterate. - Monitoring: add alert on rollback rate > threshold to pause optimistic mode for route.
open_questions: - Do we need a binary 'commit seal' with cryptographic proof to support auditable workflows for compliance-sensitive customers? - How do we version assertion schemas safely across rolling model upgrades? - Should the platform expose an 'assertion simulation' mode to preview behavior with historical sessions? - What is the recommended default assertion confidence threshold per client platform (mobile vs server)?
next_steps: 1) Align with runtime and serving teams on minimal frame envelope (1 week). 2) Prototype JS StreamCursor + AssertEvaluator with a sample chat UI (2 sprints). 3) Add tool registry prototype to internal dev console and wire demo route (2 sprints). 4) Run internal playtest with Solutions Engineering and Customer Success (1 sprint). 5) Prepare external pilot pack and SDK docs (2 sprints).
notes_to_reviewers: This is intentionally a focused sketch prioritizing ergonomics and actionable assertions over exhaustive schema coverage. Looking for feedback on: (a) actionability semantics, (b) idempotency model and parent_frame mapping, (c) sensible defaults for conservative vs optimistic modes.
references: Related internal sketches: progressive-results-declarative-plugins-prd-draft, client-side-fallback-policy-language-and-sdkspec. External inspiration: streaming JSON envelope patterns and server-sent event best practices.
legal_and_compliance_considerations: Tool calls that send customer data off-host should be gated by route-level policy and explicit KMS/consent flags. Default SDKs will mark optimistic actions as 'local-only' unless route policy permits server-side tool dispatch.
